aboutH2: Kackaamin Family Development Centre: Family Healing in Port Alberni
intro: There are male, female, youth and family sweats throughout the session. They are hosted on campus and are facilitated by our Cultural / Spiritual Coordinator. This gentle and safe place has been likened to the womb of our mother wherein much self discovery and gratitude can be found. All clients are encouraged to participate in the spiritual healing and awakening that is available in the Sweat Lodge. It is our belief that through the insertion of a 12 step support program that recovery is far more likely. There are two scheduled AA meetings weekly. One is hosted onsite at Kackaamin and one is off campus in the town of Port Alberni. All adult clients attend these on a rotating schedule that allows for childcare to be possible. Clients make meaningful connections that create a more sustainable recovery. The life skills learned in the 12 step programs through peer support are part of the foundation that is laid during our session.

pillars.title: A Forested Campus on Beaver Creek Road
pillars.body: Kackaamin moved to this site in Port Alberni in 2009, onto the territory of the Tseshaht and Hupacasath First Nations. Sixteen furnished housing units sit around a children's park, so each family has its own home base for the whole session. The rest of the campus holds the adult education building, a K-12 Learning Centre, children's centres for different ages, a gym and the places used for ceremony: a sweat, a sacred fire and an outdoor gathering space. Staff are on site around the clock.

pillars.title: Planning for Home Starts Before You Arrive
pillars.body: Kackaamin works closely with the counsellor who refers each family. Adults complete at least six one-hour pre-treatment counselling or support sessions before a session starts, and the centre only admits families who have counselling and follow-up lined up for when they get home. Family Recovery Planning is one of the workshops in the 6-week program, so families go home with a plan they built together and a counsellor ready to pick it up.

pillars.title: Elders, Counsellors and Child Care Staff
pillars.body: The Family Program team includes Elders, a cultural support worker, a master cedar weaver, registered clinical counsellors, early childhood educators and a family health lead who is a licensed practical nurse. The centre calls its care trauma informed and gives staff ongoing training to back that up. Ne'i client care workers and contractors who lead cedar weaving, yoga and integrated healing therapy work alongside them.

overviewH2: Kackaamin Family Development Centre: Programs Overview
overview: Kackaamin is one of three Indigenous family treatment programs in Canada. It began in 1974 at Kakawis on Meares Island, on the site of the former Christie Indian Residential School, after Nuu-chah-nulth Elders, the Catholic Church and local business people decided the old site should become a family centre. Today Kackaamin is an accredited non-profit society with three departments: the Core/Family Programs, a 10-bed Supportive Recovery Program for women in early recovery, and Rebuilding the Circle, which supports healing from sexual violence.
serviceCaption: 11 services · as described by the centre
afterOverview: The 6-week family program is a later-stage recovery program. Parents come with their children, ages 0 to 18, and everyone takes part in age-appropriate workshops on communication and emotions, addiction and its impact on families, complex trauma, grief and loss, and cultural oppression and lateral violence. Parents attend AA/NA, and the program teaches Nuu-chah-nulth parenting next to the Circle of Security Parenting Program. Kackaamin often practises Nuu-chah-nulth culture and teachings, and it also encourages each family to practise its own traditions, teachings and protocols.

location.heading: Kackaamin Family Development Centre in Port Alberni, British Columbia
location.intro: Kackaamin is on Beaver Creek Road in Port Alberni, in the Alberni Valley of central Vancouver Island, on Tseshaht and Hupacasath territory. From Vancouver, plan on about 4 hours with the Horseshoe Bay to Nanaimo ferry and the drive west on Highway 4; Nanaimo is about 1 hour 15 minutes away, Victoria under 3 hours, and Tofino or Ucluelet about 1 hour 45 minutes to the west.

faqIntro: Answers come from the centre's own website and public listings. Still unsure? Call, it's free and confidential.

faqs.q: Who can attend Kackaamin Family Development Centre?
faqs.a: The family program mainly serves people of First Nations ancestry and people connected to a First Nations person through marriage or a common-law relationship. Priority goes to First Nations people who live in B.C., and the centre takes a limited number of families from the Yukon each year. Non-Indigenous people can apply if they secure independent funding for every family member who attends.

faqs.q: How much does Kackaamin cost, and who pays?
faqs.a: Kackaamin does not publish a fee. If you are a B.C. resident with First Nations Health Benefits, the First Nations Health Authority (FNHA) covers the program. Without those benefits, funding may come from social assistance, EI, a Friendship Centre, an EAP or your own money, and people without status cover their own cost. Groceries are not covered, though a band, Friendship Centre or social program may help, and travel is usually paid by FNHA, Health Canada or your band.

The core family program runs for 6 weeks, plus pre-treatment and post-treatment care at home. Shorter programs, such as the Grandmothers' and Grandfathers' programs, run 1 to 2 weeks, and the length of the women's Supportive Recovery Program varies by person. The 2026 family sessions are listed as Sept 14 to Oct 16 and Nov 9 to Dec 11.

No. The family program cannot provide detox or stabilization, and families who need withdrawal support (including short-acting OAT) are not eligible. Adults need at least 6 to 8 weeks of abstinence before they arrive, and the centre suggests individual treatment first for detox needs. The centre also says it does not currently accept people on methadone.

faqs.q: How do I get referred and apply?
faqs.a: You need a referral from a professional such as an alcohol and drug counsellor, mental health counsellor, social worker or medical person, and you must have a counsellor for post-treatment care. Each family member completes an application, which is faxed to the intake team. A clinical therapist then holds an intake interview by video or phone, and an intake committee reviews the family's file. There is usually a waitlist of 1 to 2 sessions.

faqs.q: Must I have children to attend?
faqs.a: To attend the six-week family program, yes. People without children are welcome to sign up for the shorter programs (i.e. Restoring Balance, Supportive Recovery, Rebuilding the Circle).

faqs.q: Where is Kackaamin and how do I get there?
faqs.a: The centre is at 7830 Beaver Creek Rd in Port Alberni, on central Vancouver Island. From Vancouver it is about 4 hours including the BC Ferries crossing to Nanaimo, and from Nanaimo about 1 hour 15 minutes west on Highway 4. Families confirm their travel arrangements as part of the application, and travel is often funded by FNHA, Health Canada or the family's band.

faqs.q: What happens after the program ends?
faqs.a: Families go home to the counsellor who referred them, because the centre only admits families with post-treatment counselling and follow-up in place. Family Recovery Planning is part of the 6-week program, so that counsellor receives a family with a plan already worked out. Supportive Recovery clients build safe, healthy connections in the community as part of their re-integration.

faqs.q: Is Kackaamin a public or private centre?
faqs.a: Kackaamin is a non-profit society, primarily funded by Island Health, the First Nations Health Authority, the Ministry of Children and Family Development, School District #70 and Aboriginal Head Start. In October 2023 it was fully accredited with Exemplary Standing by Accreditation Canada.

faqs.q: What is the Supportive Recovery Program?
faqs.a: It is a 10-bed program at Kackaamin for women aged 19 and older in early recovery from moderate to severe substance use, which may include mild to moderate mental health concerns such as depression or anxiety. Priority goes to Nuu-chah-nulth members and to First Nations, Métis and Inuit people living in Nuu-chah-nulth territory. It includes 12 Step supports, cultural supports, individual counselling and accommodation on site, and intake is ongoing.

Rebuilding the Circle is Kackaamin's program for the impacts of sexual abuse and assault, using both western and Nuu-chah-nulth practices. It runs healing sessions for men and women who have been harmed through sexual violence, a Restoration Program for those who have harmed others sexually, and support for family systems affected by sexual harm. The RTC office is at 1-778-421-8811.
